newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end slightly firmer after 10-yr bond auction.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end slightly firmer after 10-yr bond auction.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed slightly firmer on Tuesday after the new 10-year JGB auction went as expected.
The auction produced a lowest price of 100.80 and an average price at 100.85. The lowest price was exactly what many operators had expected, traders said.

But investors did not show instant demand for the new bond, which was one factor keeping the June from rising sharply, they said. Investors were seen preferring buying the bond with the price at par if the market were to weaken from the current high levels. The June contract ended up 0.07 at 126.98.
It moved between 126.85 and 127.06 after opening at 127.00.

The Ministry of Finance (MOF) set the coupon rate for the new 10-year bond at 2.4 percent, instead of what many had expected of a rate of 2.3 percent, and this provided support to the June contract in early trade, traders said. MOF announced the new bond offer at 8.30 a.m. (2330 GMT Monday).
"There was decent demand for the new bond from a variety of investors because the coupon rate was better than what many had expected," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank's securities unit.

A dealer at a "Big Four" brokerage house echoed that view: "We see no difficulty in selling the new 10-year JGB because consistent buying is expected when the bond price falls close to par (in the secondary market)."
Daiwa Securities and Nomura Securities were the two biggest bidders for the bond. Their bids accounted for about 40 percent of the accepted bids of 591.19 billion yen, traders said.

"It may take time before the new bond is sold out. But if the June contract falls to around 126.75, investors' buying may emerge because that is equivalent to a price of par for the new bond," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.

Investors were also not in a hurry to buy the new bond with government-backed and municipal bonds to be launched on Wednesday and Tokyo Electric Power's long-term straight expected to be launched this week.
Traders said the June JGB futures' upside was capped above 127.00 due to uncertainties ahead of BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita's news conference on Wednesday.

They said JGBs retained their firmness from last week when falls were limited despite a remark by MOF official Eisuke Sakakibara that the JGB market was "bubbly". But a change in Matsushita's tone on the economy would be far more important.
Activity was slow in the cash JGB market, traders said.
Some small-lot selling was detected from dealers in JGBs with five to seven years remaining until maturity to replace them with the new 10-year bond, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.125 percent at 0752 GMT, down from 2.150 percent on Monday.
